title: Large language models empowered agent-based modeling and simulation: a survey and perspectives
publisher: Humanities and Social Sciences Communications (Palgrave/Nature Portfolio)

key_points.claim: Survey organizes LLM-empowered ABMS by domain (cyber, physical, social, hybrid) and by four challenges: environment perception, human alignment, action generation, evaluation.
key_points.evidence_quote: challenges in environment perception, human alignment, action generation, and evaluation

key_points.claim: Traditional ABMS methodology moved from knowledge-driven (predefined rules such as cellular automata, symbolic equations such as social force model) to data-driven (stochastic, machine learning) approaches.
key_points.evidence_quote: the former includes various approaches based on predefined rules or symbolic equations, and the latter includes stochastic models and machine learning models

key_points.claim: Social-domain ABMS covers social interaction (networks, communities, organizations, opinion dynamics, crowds) and economic systems (markets, financial interactions).
key_points.evidence_quote: social interaction that focuses on social networks, community interactions, or organizational behavior

key_points.claim: Limitation of traditional ABM: reactive architectures dominate because deliberative symbolic models are intractable; agents are weak at long-term planning and do not generalize across environments.
key_points.evidence_quote: optimizing the internal world model and planning-reasoning module based on symbolical AI approaches are generally intractable in practice

key_points.claim: No single traditional method supports description, explanation, prediction and scenario exploration together (rules descriptive, symbolic/stochastic explanatory, ML predictive but less interpretable).
key_points.evidence_quote: existing methods cannot support the above tasks simultaneously

key_points.claim: Heterogeneity in traditional ABM is hard: parameter calibration is complex, data scarce, and rules cannot cover all dimensions, leading to oversimplification. LLM agents offer human-like internal complexity and customization via prompting, in-context learning, fine-tuning.
key_points.evidence_quote: specialized and customized characteristics with prompting, in-context learning, or fine-tuning

key_points.claim: Environments for LLM agent societies are virtual (sandboxes like Smallville in Generative Agents, virtual software company, RecAgent) or real (EconAgent macroeconomics, WebAgent, Urban Generative Intelligence). Interfaces are mostly text-based.
key_points.evidence_quote: builds a Smallville sandbox world in which large language model-empowered agents plan their days, share news, form relationships, and coordinate group activities

key_points.claim: Agent communication is mainly textual (direct) or indirect via rules (e.g., economic rules linking workers in a factory); multimodality and tools are expanding interfaces.
key_points.evidence_quote: the agents can indirectly interact with others through predefined rules

key_points.claim: Alignment/personalization done via prompt engineering (personas, professions, preferences such as cooperative/selfish) or fine-tuning; LLM-generated feedback was reported as 45x cheaper than crowd workers for alignment.
key_points.evidence_quote: achieve high human alignment 45× cheaper than hiring crowd workers

key_points.claim: LLM agents still lack domain knowledge and can make irrational decisions; controllable heterogeneity is a key challenge.
key_points.evidence_quote: agents based on LLMs still lack the necessary domain knowledge in specific areas, leading to irrational decisions

key_points.claim: Action generation relies on planning (task decomposition, e.g. GITM, Voyager, AdaPlanner), memory (external store beyond context window) and reflection.
key_points.evidence_quote: a memory system that functions as an external database for LLM agents
